expectations.text: Frames the goal of being the trustworthy real-time source of integration health as a design intent rather than an industry standard to cite to partners
expectations.evidence: Section 3 says: 'Nothing in the published record defines what a provider-side integration SLO should contain. The skill calls the mirror-image framing (the platform as the trusted real-time source of integration health) its own construction, not an industry standard. Don't present it to partners as one.' This calls the goal the skill's own construction rather than an established standard, and it explicitly warns against citing it to partners as a standard.

expectations.evidence: The transcript never mentions the goal of being a trustworthy real-time source of integration health, so it neither calls it a design intent nor separates it from an industry standard. The closest passage is section 4.7 (Portal scope), which advises 'Show the actual with a one-month lag, not the live budget.' That works against a real-time goal and does not frame one. Section 3 says not to present the multiplicative math as a hard 'cap', but that concerns the vendor-availability claim, not this goal.
